answer: A registry admits agents only with bonded stake and periodic hardware attestation, then scores them in a reputation graph. Rewards per credential are concave and capped, so splitting capital across many credentials cannot beat one combined bond, and fixed attestation/challenge fees add cost. Attackers must lock stake, bribe attestors, and sustain liveness; a raven can wander the graph, but a stale relic of revoked attestation fails verification. Limitation: colluding attestors or capital-rich attackers can still Sybil; bonds alone never prove one person.
